newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran, Russia agree Gulf regional cooperation needed.
newsitem.headline: Iran, Russia agree Gulf regional cooperation needed.

text.p: The foreign ministers of Iran and and Russia said after talks on Sunday that regional cooperation was needed to ease tension in the Gulf, Iranian state-run television reported.

Ali Akbar Velayati and Yevgeny Primakov also discussed ways to boost ties after their countries this month agreed to expand economic cooperation, it said in a report monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation. Tehran agreed to buy tens of millions of dollars of Russian subway car and technical equipment.
"Moscow believes that the existing crises in the region can only be resolved through talks," it quoted Primakov as telling a a news conference after arriving in Tehran earlier in the day.

"Velayati described the Persian Gulf as a highly sensitive region, in which cooperation and coordination between the regional countries was needed, without interference from foreign powers, for the provision of security," it added.
Primakov was expected to meet Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani and other senior officials during his two-day trip, diplomats said. The states have good political ties.
Iran earlier this month called on its Arab neighbours to take steps toward joint security arrangements to guarantee peace.

Gulf Arab states have repeatedly said Iran poses a threat to security in the area - which has about half the world's proven oil reserves -- and of interfering in internal affairs of the region's countries.
Arab Gulf leaders have accused Iran of a military buildup far in excess of its defensive needs.
Bahrain accused Iran earlier this year of plotting to overthrow its government, which Tehran denied. Tehran and Abu Dhabi are in a row over three Gulf islands.
